correctness.rationale: For odd P and an external odd prime r, direct block counting with exact two-exclusion bijections proves T(Pr)=(r-1)S(P)/2+T(P)-2B_P(r) and S(Pr)=(r-2)S(P). This derives the residue identity without numerical inference. Complete finite gcd enumeration proves spectra (48 and 96 reduced classes), explicit witness residue lists, and the fixed-support minima, checked by an independent Python standard-library implementation (7020 integer checks). Dirichlet and fixed-modulus PNT give prime infinitude and class densities; source Theorem 3 supplies the existing uniform bound. The code was run successfully; no computation is substituted for an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The closest 2026 primary text proves the bound but not its sharpness or complete distribution. The present two-sided infinite family of squarefree extremizers, exact residue spectra and smallest fixed supports are strict conclusions not implied by an upper bound. Independent targeted mathematical-result queries and deduplication found no implication-covering stronger record; uncertainty remains for implicit prior deductions.
residual_risks: A classical inclusion-exclusion or generalized totient argument may contain the extremal-family statement implicitly in a source not discovered.
Database coverage and citation search are not an exhaustive novelty proof.

value.rationale: The problem is motivated by the exact quality of a specific published uniform error estimate. Demonstrating both endpoints on positive-density prime families proves optimality even on squarefree 3-prime integers. The two full finite prime-class distributions and minimal fixed two-prime supports explain the extremality mechanism rather than just producing isolated equalities, and give natural benchmark invariants for further totient study.
